h1: CDL General Knowledge Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any CDL general knowledge question for an instant, explained answer — air brakes, vehicle inspection, and federal rules, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: CDL General Knowledge Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free CDL General Knowledge practice test questions with instant, explained answers. Federal FMCSA rules on vehicle inspection, safe driving, hours of service, and air brakes.
whyItWorks: The General Knowledge test is built on federal FMCSA regulations (49 CFR Part 383) that nearly every state's written CDL permit exam draws from, but the material covers a lot of narrow, specific rules — pre-trip inspection steps, air brake system components, hours-of-service limits — that are easy to mix up under pressure. Cambo reads the exact question and explains the specific federal rule or safe-driving principle behind the correct answer.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the minimum passing score required on a CDL knowledge test under federal regulation?
sampleQuestions.a: 80% — 49 CFR 383.135 requires every state to set the passing score at correctly answering at least 80% of the questions on each knowledge test.

sampleQuestions.q: During a pre-trip inspection, a driver finds the low air pressure warning device activates before the pressure drops below 60 psi. What should the driver do?
options: Continue the trip as normal, since the warning is just a precaution
Not drive the vehicle until it's fixed
Drive slower than usual to compensate
Only avoid using the brakes until pressure rises
sampleQuestions.a: The driver should not operate the vehicle until it's repaired — a properly functioning low air pressure warning is a critical safety system, and driving with a known air brake problem is unsafe and a violation.

sampleQuestions.q: How does hydroplaning affect a commercial vehicle, and what should a driver do to help prevent it?
options: It only affects vehicles going under 20 mph; slow down further to avoid it
It happens when tires lose contact with the road on a film of water; reduce speed, especially in the first minutes of rain
It only occurs with empty trailers; keeping trailers loaded prevents it
It cannot happen to vehicles with good tire tread
sampleQuestions.a: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride up on a layer of water and lose contact with the road; reducing speed — particularly during the first rain after a dry spell, when oils rise to the road surface — reduces the risk.

sampleQuestions.q: Under federal hours-of-service rules for property-carrying drivers, what is the maximum number of hours a driver may drive after coming on duty following 10 consecutive hours off duty?
options: 8 hours
10 hours
11 hours
14 hours
sampleQuestions.a: 11 hours — a property-carrying driver may drive a maximum of 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty, within the broader 14-hour on-duty window.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the correct action if a commercial vehicle's brakes fail while going down a steep grade?
options: Shift into neutral and coast to slow down
Pump the brakes repeatedly to try to rebuild pressure, then use an escape ramp or runaway lane if available
Turn off the engine immediately to stop the vehicle
Accelerate to gain enough control to steer off the grade
sampleQuestions.a: Pump the brakes to try to build pressure and use an escape ramp or runaway lane if one is available and brakes don't recover — shifting to neutral or cutting the engine removes engine braking and control, making things worse.

sampleQuestions.q: What should a driver check for as part of a proper pre-trip inspection of the vehicle's tires?
options: Tread depth, sidewall condition, and matching tire types on the same axle
Only that the tires are the correct brand
Only tire pressure — tread and sidewalls are checked at annual inspection only
Nothing — tire condition is the responsibility of the maintenance shop only
sampleQuestions.a: Tread depth, sidewall condition (cuts, bulges, exposed cords), and that mismatched tire types (e.g., radial and bias-ply) aren't mixed on the same axle — all are required pre-trip checks, and the driver is responsible for catching them before driving.

faqs.q: How many questions are on the CDL General Knowledge test?
faqs.a: Federal rules set a minimum of 30 questions, but most states use a longer General Knowledge test form, commonly 50 questions.

faqs.q: What score do I need to pass?
faqs.a: 80% — federal regulation (49 CFR 383.135) requires every state to set this same passing threshold on each CDL knowledge test.

faqs.q: Do I need to pass other knowledge tests besides General Knowledge?
faqs.a: It depends on the class of CDL and any endorsements you're pursuing. Everyone takes General Knowledge; driving a vehicle with air brakes requires the Air Brakes test, combination vehicles (like a tractor-trailer) require the Combination Vehicles test, and endorsements like Hazmat, Passenger, School Bus, or Tanker each have their own additional test.

faqs.q: How many times can I retake the test if I fail?
faqs.a: Most states allow multiple attempts, but a mandatory waiting period between attempts (commonly a few days to a week) and any cap on total tries before reapplying vary by state — check your state's DMV or licensing agency for exact rules.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the FMCSA or any state DMV?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration or any state motor vehicle agency.

faqs.q: What are the basic prerequisites to take the CDL knowledge test?
faqs.a: Requirements vary by state, but generally include holding a valid regular driver's license, meeting minimum age requirements (18 for intrastate driving, 21 for interstate or hazmat), and passing a DOT medical exam to hold a valid medical certificate.
